**What you'll do**

1. Read what the Shure SM57 is.
2. Learn how it hears: pattern, proximity, off axis.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Look up famous uses.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- The **SM57** came out in **1965** (Wikipedia, "Shure SM57"): a **dynamic** mic (a coil on a diaphragm in a magnet), **cardioid**.
- Range **40-15,000 Hz** with a **presence rise** (Shure). Sensitivity **-56 dBV/Pa** (Wikipedia): quiet output, so it needs gain.
- Its forerunner, the Unidyne 545, was on Brian Wilson's vocals on *Pet Sounds*; every US president since Johnson has spoken through one (Wikipedia).

## How it hears

- **Cardioid**: loudest in front, nearly deaf behind: aim its back at what you do not want (the hi-hat).
- Close up, a directional mic gains **bass**: the **proximity effect** (Wikipedia, "Proximity effect (audio)"). Slide the distance and watch the low end of the graph rise.
- The response graph is the maker's published chart **digitised approximately** (the charts are pictures; the points here follow their shape as remembered: unverified).
- No published max SPL: a dynamic takes a snare or a loud amp at a few centimetres.

## The mic

The Shure SM57 drawn after photos (proportions approximate, no logos). Drag the blue mic in the room (or use the Distance slider; the wheel or Angle turns it), choose a source and a room, press **▶ Hear it**. Voice is generated (the band has no singer); snare and kick are the band's kit; the guitar is the site's amp model. Nobody has compared the sound with a real mic.

```{=html}
<div class="mic" data-mic="sm57" data-src="snare"></div>
```

## Works Cited

<!-- works-cited: written by scripts/works-cited.py -->
::: {.works-cited}
"Microphone." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microphone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microphone). Polar patterns as first-order sums: the cardioid = omni + figure-8, the figure-8's negative rear signal cancelling; ribbons' symmetric front and rear pickup.

"Shure SM57." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shure_SM57](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shure_SM57). 1965; -56.0 dBV/Pa; 150 ohm rated (300 actual); Unidyne 545 on Pet Sounds vocals; vocal users incl. Tom Waits; every US president since LBJ.

"SM57 Dynamic Instrument Microphone." *Shure*, [www.shure.com/en-US/products/microphones/sm57](https://www.shure.com/en-US/products/microphones/sm57). Accessed 26 Nov. 2026. Cardioid dynamic; 40-15,000 Hz; "contoured frequency response" with a presence rise.

**For students**

"Proximity effect (audio)." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proximity_effect_(audio)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proximity_effect_(audio)). Bass rises close to a directional mic; caused by the ports; not a true omni, but not necessarily absent on a multipattern mic's summed omni.
:::
<!-- /works-cited -->
